subject: Canopy AI — privacy constraints & short-horizon storage options (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@canopy.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & options from today's call — Canopy AI privacy constraints

Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap from discovery
- Primary use case: conversation summarization for customer-support transcripts (PII possible: names, emails, order numbers).
- Desired hard requirement: Canopy needs either (A) route-level 0-retention for the sensitive endpoint, or (B) a short-horizon store (<=7 days) with strict isolation and audit logs.
- Secondary ask: SOC 2 type II evidence, per-route encryption (customer KMS preferred), and the ability to surface deletion/audit records on demand.

Options we can offer (short summary — attached doc has more detail):
1) 0-retention (session-only) — Redwood does not persist the conversation transcript or KV cache to long-term storage. Transactions handled in-memory/KV cache and discarded at session close. Works best if you can accept no post-hoc replay.
2) Short-horizon TTL (configurable per-route) — TTL values available: 4 hours / 24 hours / 7 days. Data kept encrypted at rest, separate tenant pools for Dedicated customers, and per-route audit events.
3) Hybrid: store non-PII artifacts (embeddings/metadata) for longer but redact or truncate PII fields; PII tokens mapped into ephemeral handles stored only during session.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Please confirm which option you'd like us to scope for a firm proposal (0-retention, 24h, 7d, or hybrid).
- If 0-retention is required only for a subset of endpoints, list those endpoints so we can scope routing and cost impact.
- We'll loop in Security (Stephanie) and Sales Eng (Ben) for a short technical call to finalize PII scoping and SOC 2 evidence.

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-options.pdf, Canopy-MAP.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Samira — great questions. Short answers inline, expanded below.

> 1) For 0-retention: can you confirm that no logs, transcripts, or KV snapshots will be written to disk or S3-equivalents?
Short: yes for the session path we described — transcripts and per-request payloads are not persisted to long-term storage. They are kept in an encrypted in-memory/KV cache during the session and cleared at session close. (Stephanie included more technical detail below.)

> 2) For the TTL options: if we pick 24h, can we have a self-service route to trigger deletion earlier for individual sessions?
Yes — we support per-session deletion via an API call (delete-session) and through the Console. We'll include the API spec in the follow-up pack.

> 3) Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys in Hosted mode, or is that only for Private/Dedicated?
We support CMKs in Dedicated and Private today. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key via partner-managed KMS in select regions; we can evaluate a short pilot if CMK is a blocker.

> 4) SOC2 evidence — can you share the current summary and how frequently Redwood rotates the independent auditor?
Attached: SOC2-summary-2025.pdf. Our latest audit is 2025 and we run annual audits; we can provide a scope summary and an auditor letter on NDA.

Stephanie — tagging you for the technical confirmation and one-paragraph architecture note we can share with Canopy security. Ben — can you prepare a short cost delta for 0-retention per million tokens vs 7d retention?

Proposed tech sync slots: Wed 09/30 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 10/01 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works for you and Canopy security?

—
Marissa

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: 0-retention & per-route TTL — short architecture note
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Marissa / Canopy — brief note you can share: 
- 0-retention route: requests are routed to a transient execution pool. No request/response bodies are written to persistent blob storage; KV caches used for decoding are kept in encrypted memory-backed stores attached to GPUs and cleared on session termination.
- Short-horizon TTL: data is written to encrypted object storage with a per-object TTL tag. Background job enforces TTL deletion across tenant buckets; deletion events are logged to an audit stream with request IDs.
- Deletion API: synchronous delete-session endpoint removes session artifacts and emits an audit event (ID returned).
- Keys: customer KMS (CMK) supported in Dedicated/Private; Hosted support is region-limited and requires partner KMS integration.

Limitations / legal notes: for complete zero-knowledge (no telemetry), we need to agree on a contract addendum for telemetry/monitoring carveouts (SLA and incident handling implications).

From: Samira Khan <samira@canopy.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

- Requirements: we will need (A) the one-paragraph architecture note in writing for our security review, (B) a redlined addendum that specifies telemetry carveouts and incident response expectations, and (C) SOC2 auditor letter under NDA.

We can do the tech sync on Thu 10/01 09:00 PT — Samir (our security lead) will join. After that call we'll expect a short proposal with cost delta, contract addendum draft, and an example API call for delete-session (so our SREs can validate).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
